answer: In an AI agent marketplace funding lagoon restoration, each identity must lock $100 for 90 days before it can submit bids, and each stake backs only one identity at a time. The bond acts as an anchor: an attacker growing a trellis of 10,000 fake agents must immobilize $1 million, paying financing or opportunity costs throughout the lockup. Creating new keys is cheap, but activating them at scale consumes scarce capital.
